newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Increased competition seen in EU insurance industry.
newsitem.headline: Increased competition seen in EU insurance industry.

text.p: Competition has increased in the European Union's insurance industry following the launch of the single market, the EU's statistics office Eurostat said on Thursday.

In a survey of the European insurance industry in 1995, Eurostat said data indicated "a marked increase in the pressure of competition in some member states" and that this called for thorough rationalisation measures which would lower costs.

There were just over 4,000 insurance companies in Switzerland and the 18-nation European Economic Area, which consists of the EU, Norway, Iceland and Liechtenstein, a figure that had declined slightly in almost all countries.
"The marked increase in competition in the wake of deregulation and opening up of the markets obviously forced a number of enterprises to cease trading," Eurostat said.

"The fact that in the new environment it is much easier to set up new enterprises has not yet managed to offset this trend," it said in a statement, adding however that the number of firms had increased in Spain, Luxembourg and Ireland.
The report identified the insurance sectors in Germany and Luxembourg as "particularly profitable".
In most EU member states non-life insurance had a combined ratio -- claims incurred plus operating expenses as a percentage of direct premiums written -- of 95 percent.
"In 1995 this ratio for Germany was just over 90 percent, for Luxembourg a little under 88 percent and for Iceland 84 percent," Eurostat said.

In the non-life area the European insurance industry performed well compared with the U.S. sector. "It is also notable that Luxembourg further strengthened its already strong position as a reinsurance centre," it said.

Motor vehicle insurance was in the forefront of non-life business. However, "there was a striking decrease in the percentage of motor vehicle insurance in hitherto highly- regulated markets such as Germany and Austria where the effect of pressure on premium rates was greater than in other areas of non-life business."
"In markets which have already been deregulated for some time, such as the U.K. and the Netherlands there is no such pressure on prices," Eurostat added.
The relative importance of accident and health insurance was increasing in almost all countries. "This reflects the structural change in state social security systems."

In contrast to non-life insurance, there was an upward trend in life insurance in most EEA countries. "As a result of demographic pressures on state old-age pension schemes many people take out additional private insurance," it said.
The EU's single market was launched in 1993 but the last legislation concerning insurance industry liberalisation came into force only on July 1, 1994. -- Brussels newsroom +32 2 287 68 11
